newsitem.title: USA: Conn. small business group seeks gasoline tax cut.
newsitem.headline: Conn. small business group seeks gasoline tax cut.

text.p: Connecticut small-business owners want to see the state's motor fuels tax reduced, according to a survey released Wednesday by the state's leading small-business advocacy group.

"Not only did we have the distinction of having the highest motor fuels tax last year at 38 cents per gallon, (but) we hit a new mark January 1 when the rate went to 39 cents," said Armando Paolino, state director of the 5,000-member National Federation of Independent Business Connecticut chapter.
Paolino noted in a statement that 12 cents of the 38 cents went to operations and fringe benefits, "not the dedicated use for road and bridge construction, as originally designed."
Legislation to lower the gasoline tax is at the top of the Federation's agenda, said Paolino.
Connecticut Governor John Rowland, a Republican, has called for cutting the state's gas tax.
But Connecticut Comptroller Nancy Wyman, the state's chief financial officer, said Wednesday the state should think hard about any new tax cuts.
Wyman, a Democrat, told a news conference on Wednesday that Connecticut has nearly $700 million in tax cuts on the books that will be in place by the end of the 1999 budget year.
"We must view these tax reduction obligations in light of an overall state operating position that is still in deficit and still relies heavily on debt financing," she said.

"I recommend that the governor and the legislature assess the impact of the tax cuts currently in place before creating any new ones and prioritize any tax cuts so that they assist the greatest number of Connecticut's citizens," she added.
